prompt: On a number line, $x > 3$ has an open or closed circle at $3$?
hint: Ask yourself whether $3$ itself makes the statement true. Is $3$ greater than $3$?

hints.text: Ask yourself whether $3$ itself makes the statement true. Is $3$ greater than $3$?
The symbol $>$ means strictly greater, so $3$ is not part of the solution. Which kind of circle shows a number that is left out?
Because $3$ is not included, the circle at $3$ is open.

explanation: The inequality $x > 3$ means $x$ is greater than $3$, with no "or equal to".
Test the endpoint: $3 > 3$ is false, so $3$ is not a solution.
A number that is left out is drawn with an empty circle, so the circle at $3$ is open.
